Hey, so this is what we're gonna do when the min/max parameter for fire icon does not return a fire icon. If for example the parameter is set as 2-3 and nothing returns

record.title: Optimization for Fake Shadows
record.body:
Instead of running on Update, now the material updates are done on demand, only while the tile is animating.

On the tween manager, I created an event to let the shadows know that an animation will start. The shadows check if the animation will execute on their tile or not. If it is on their tile, they start updating the material color until the animation is done.

A couple minor changes were added as well.

record.title: Improving client-server request management
record.body: -Handling initial loading requests with retry. -Added request blockers -Added batch system for requests, now you need to commit changes to sync to the server. -- commits are done on specific moments such as end level or when exit a mini game. I left a few logs so it is clear when a sync is happening. There are many request such as requesting time and live ops that are behaving as before, no special handling. More work in needed on that front. This needs lots of testing. What can go wrong ? - Probably data not being saved because a missing commit. I tested normal game and mini games, also upgrading Sophie, but I probably missed something... A consequence of moving everything to the end of the level is that players can quit the app before finishing a level to avoid losing money/lives... I need to think how to handle that..

record.body:
Created a robust blob system to store quest information and stop relying on the server so much. Quest information is now stored in the persistent data path and is retrieved from the server only in specific times (when new quests are generated from the server).
This system will solve most of the UI bugs that were related to server synchronization, including the new quest alert bug, keys not matching the real value, issues when swapping between quest categories, etc.
This still needs a little bit of testing so in the meanwhile I'm setting it as draft, but the reviews can start.

record.title: fixing issues when moving from end of chapter 2 to chapter 3
record.body: This is a long story.. First I started testing the issue, obviously it didn't happen on editor but we did have a few errors showing up. Precisely on chapter 3 level 1 there is a tutorial showing you how to select a different character. This tutorial was not working (Only if you reload the game) But why would this tutorial be related to the chapter end screen null exception? Well.. I noticed that the PostLevelQueueManager always checks the ends screen calling its init function, but it does after the tutorial has called ProcessNextEvent, my theory is that since the tutorial was throwing an exception, ProcessNextEvent was not being called leaving the Init call to chapter end screen in the queue. With the broken tutorial you are able to click through it getting into the board scene, eventually another tutorial code ends up calling ProcessNextEvent, causing the pending call to be executed in the board scene. In the board scene the chapter end screen no longer exists, causing the exception. I was able to verify that this was indeed happening in the order I described, but in editor I didn't get an exception (how game objects are destroyed when a scene in unloaded is not predictable) So.. I focused my attention on the tutorial issue. This is the expected behavior: And it was a tricky bug.. why was the tutorial not finding the correct button... The reason lies on how the Harmony Games button registers and unregisters.. it uses an id.. In the code buttons are being instantiated and the id is being set, but.. the button registers itself on the awake, setting the id after instantiation is too late. item.GetComponent()._buttonID = "CharacterSelectPrelevel"; Even worse, changing the id after instantiation causes it to fail to unregister, since it is trying to unregister with the changed id. This code was leaking references. The tutorial was picking one of those zombie references. There are two places where this is being done (setting the id after instantiation) I have not check if the other one is causing issues.. but I will check later. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a753d57b-fda5-4b9e-8864-1c067e9e7d09

record.title: Fixes to queue manager
record.body: The main issue was that Nathans win streak code had code paths that would not call ProcessNextEvent, causing the queue to get stuck. Ideally we should move Nathans win streak to the level end, instead of doing it here. It also takes some time for the avatar and everything to actually move because it is waiting for a request related to Nathans wins streak to finish. Ideally nothing in the PostLevelQueueManager should block. Also post level queue manager with stuck events is dangerous, because those events end up trying to trigger on a different scene. (chaos) There are other problems that are I found that don't help. The first time user experience tutorials are very easy to break, if you skip one or related the next tutorials trigger in wrong order and I didn't find a way to recover.. why don't we make the tutorials require a specific level to trigger? With this changes, if you don't skip tutorials/reload the game.. everything seems to work fine. One interesting bit is that the function that is supposed to return the last chapter number, is actually returning and index, starting from 0. I had to change to requirement. public const int NatesWinStreakUnlockChapter = 3; public const int NatesWinStreakUnlockChapterIndex = 2;

record.title: person_6065/addressables improvement march 7
record.body: I open this PR not exactly expecting it to be merged. It is more about starting a conversation on what we can do. And the best way is to show some working changes. This PR focuses on removing the biggest offender when creating asset bundles, which is the "WorldMapUI.prefab". That prefabs add like 40 mb of assets to an asset bundle. Some of the assets that are referenced by that prefab are: ![image](https://github.com/harmonygames-Games/GameOfDominoes/assets/703726/67f94f83-daff-4524-b2c5-4ec6f825fd4f) After moving it back to the main build this are the results. ![Screenshot 2024-03-07 at 16 54 53](https://github.com/harmonygames-Games/GameOfDominoes/assets/703726/3bfd59b0-1768-40e7-a830-643836dbdac3) I am loading it using Resources.Load For the moment I chose to do the simplest approach because dealing with the WorldMapUI.prefab is not a trivial task. The problems I see and I am sure you are aware of are: - Most of the UI is packed in there, which is not very flexible among other issues. - Uses those really big Sophie and Nathan models (Probably those could be explicitly loaded from an asset bundle), btw. I did look up why they were so heavy, having the blend keys stuff looks nice but it does have a price. The consequences: - I removed the WorldMapUI.prefab from every scene, if someone wants to work with it, they will have to drop it in the scene. Other thoughts: I thought other ways to handle the WorldMapUI.prefab. - "adding an extra scene and loading the chapter additive ?" -> doesn't solve anything. - "putting the prefab in a asset bundle and reference it?" -> helps with the build size, but doesn't seem like a complete solution, I personally think that prefab needs to be broken down. But if we can't handle the increased build size at this moment, it is an option. what do you think?, Do you have any other ideas ? Conclusions: Since leaving the WorldMapUI.prefab in the Resources folder is not a complete solution. We should plan what to do with it A few extra changes: I added a package that shows the contents of buildlayout.txt Also I added a package to work with rider in the project.. that is my preferred editor for the moment, is it ok to include it ?

record.body: This is related to the renaming puzzles tasks. One of the requirements was to renamed puzzles that are removed from a pack and I forgot that feature. The idea here is that you can remove puzzles from a pack and those puzzles are registered on a dictionary. If you save the pack, all the removed puzzles are renamed to orphaned_{old_name}_{pack_name}_{rnd}, the last bit is to avoid collisions with previously renamed files. In the case you remove a puzzle but don't save the file, puzzles are not renamed. And that seems to work fine with the puzzle editor. ok, this is the logic behind this changes!

At first I thought that I needed to move the event that triggers the count down to a moment before doing the match. 
Because as it was, first the match would happen and the vanishing tile would flip and then the player action would count affecting the vanishing tile that was just revealed. 
But that was breaking the rewind... but not just that!
With the event that triggers the count down happening first there was a case where clicking a red vanishing would trigger it, and I am mostly sure you should be able to match a red vanishing tile.
So I did the following changes instead.

record.body:
Changed logic of tiles validation during explosion.

Previously all tiles affected by radius were included. Now affected tile should either have all parents and all children affected as well or have no child/parent tiles, only then it could be valid for explosion.

I also removed previous logic which was aimed to keep tiles unopened if their parent was exploded.

record.title: ENG-1112 Rewinding hand tile has weird animation - tile returning to the pile rotates first.
record.body:
I moved _onPileChange event call before hand-to-pile (if it placed after hand-to-pile animation it causes queuing unnecessary rotation animations for every pile tile which lead to visual issues). Also removed RecalculateExtraTilesInHandPile call (it's called during _onPileChange event anyway, unnecessary duplication).
Unfortunately, the order of calling animation methods is important (because animations could be queued incorrectly).
Also adjusted hand-to-pile animation a bit (while rewinding tiles moved to the right somehow, looks buggy), but can revert if it's on purpose.

record.title: Fixed bundle tile duplicated rewards
record.body:
https://linear.app/harmonygames-games/issue/ENG-1257/bundle-tile-doubles-tile-rewards-in-train-levels-when-exploded
Actually, only was bomb is required. Multiple bombs don't affect the outcome.
The issue is caused by multiple calls to the flip functions..
Instead of trying to think how to avoid flip to be called multiple times I opted to use Idempotence. The bundle tile can only be consumed once. 

1 flip was because of the bomb, the second one was because the bundle tile was under something that exploded.
